scenes.heading: Alerting Design
scenes.narration: Good alerting wakes you only for problems worth waking up for, and fighting alert fatigue is what keeps those alerts trustworthy.

scenes.heading: Symptoms of alert fatigue
bullets: Responders start ignoring or muting alerts
Too many pages fire for non-actionable events
Real incidents get lost in the noise
Trust in the alerting system erodes
scenes.narration: Alert fatigue sets in when responders begin ignoring or muting notifications out of self-defense. It grows when pages fire for events nobody can act on. The real danger is that a genuine incident gets buried in the noise, and once trust in the system erodes, even good alerts get dismissed.

scenes.heading: Symptom vs cause alerts
scenes.narration: Alerting on symptoms means paging only when users would actually feel the impact, such as a freshness objective being breached. Alerting on every internal cause floods responders with hiccups that often heal themselves. Symptom-based alerting produces fewer but far more meaningful pages.

scenes.heading: An alert rule with a burn threshold
scenes.code:
groups:
  - name: data-freshness
    rules:
      - alert: PipelineFreshnessBreach
        expr: (time() - pipeline_last_success_ts) > 3600
        for: 10m
        labels:
          severity: page
        annotations:
          summary: "Serving table stale > 1h"
          runbook: "https://wiki/runbooks/freshness"
scenes.narration: This rule fires only when the pipeline has been stale for more than an hour, matching a real freshness objective. The ten-minute duration clause suppresses transient blips that would otherwise page needlessly. Attaching a severity and a runbook link means the alert arrives already actionable.

scenes.heading: Tuning the alert set
scenes.narration: Tuning starts by reviewing how often each alert pages and whether anyone acted on it. Non-actionable alerts get deleted rather than muted. Adding duration windows and sensible thresholds cuts flapping, and routing by severity sends only true emergencies to the pager.

scenes.text: If an alert doesn't require a human to act right now, it belongs on a dashboard — not on the pager.
scenes.narration: If an alert does not demand that a human act right now, it belongs on a dashboard rather than on the pager.
